t: Listen to a talk in an ecology class.
When two species live in close contact, we call it symbiosis.
But symbiosis comes in three forms, depending on who benefits.
Clownfish and sea anemones are a good example.
The anemone's stinging tentacles protect the clownfish from predators, and the clownfish, in return, chases away fish that would eat the anemone.
In commensalism, one species benefits and the other is basically unaffected.
Barnacles attach themselves to the skin of whales.
The barnacles get a free ride to waters full of food, and the whale doesn't really gain or lose anything.
Here one species benefits at the expense of the other.
A tick feeding on a deer's blood is a parasite.
Notice that both commensal organisms and parasites live on their hosts.
The difference is whether the host is harmed.
